chunks: And a group informed me from Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, who said: A group from the people of Qom, among them Ali ibn Babawayh, narrated to me: A group from the people of Qom, among them Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Imran al-Saffar and his relative, the lady al-Saffar, and al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, may Allah have mercy on them, said: We were present in Baghdad in the year in which my father, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh, passed away. And Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri, may his soul be sanctified, would ask us frequently about the news of Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on him). We would say: Letters have come stating he is well. Until came the day on which he was taken (died). He asked us about him, and we mentioned to him the same thing. He said to us: May Allah reward you regarding Ali ibn al-Husayn, for he has been taken (died) at this hour. They said: We recorded the date of the hour, the day, and the month. Then, after seventeen or eighteen days, news came that he had been taken (died) in that very hour which the Shaykh Abu al-Hasan (may his soul be sanctified) had mentioned.

key_terms.قُدِّسَ سِرُّهُ: May his soul be sanctified (honorific for the Imam's companion)

ai.seo_question: How did the companions verify the death of Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa through the Imam's companion?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the role of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Samuri as the deputy of the Twelfth Imam during the Minor Occultation, illustrating his ability to receive divine news regarding the passing of prominent scholars like Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh. The precise confirmation of the death hour underscores the spiritual authority and *ismah*-adjacent knowledge attributed to the Imam’s representatives, reinforcing the continuity of religious guidance during the period of concealment.
